By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
43 of 2023 at Police Station Bansgaon, District Gorakhpur under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 26.01.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 24.05.2023.

The following arguments made by Sri Ravi Shankar Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Sunil Yadav, learned counsel holding brief of Sri Yashpal Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Shravan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant never tortured or harassed the deceased.
3. The deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions even over trivial issues.
4. On the fateful day, after an argument with a member of the family, the deceased consumed some noxious substance in a fit of rage.
5. The applicant did not administer any poison or noxious substance to the deceased.
6. The postmortem report opines that the cause of death could not ascertained.
7. No antemortem injuries are depicted in the postmortem report.
8. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Ajay Sharma @ Majnoo be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number,
on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
